# Investigation: `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py` size

Scope note: this document is investigation only. It does not propose a
decomposition, an order of work, or any code change.

## What the code does today

`apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py` is 1582 lines (VERIFIED,
`wc -l apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py`). Its module docstring states its
role directly: "Internal composition root - wires adapters to domain
handlers. Consolidates the duplicated factory-call patterns from CLI and
dashboard into a single location. All v1 module functions use these helpers
to obtain properly-configured domain handlers and projections."
(apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1-6, VERIFIED).

It is one `def`/`class`/`async def` list of ~55 top-level symbols (VERIFIED,
`grep -n "^def \|^class \|^async def "`). Grouped by what they wire:

- **Projection/store bootstrap**: `ensure_connected` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:114), `disconnect` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:119), `get_projection_mgr` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:124), `_build_session_store` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:129), `_build_workspace_telemetry_env` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:150), `get_execution_processor` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:172).
- **Agent command building**: `_build_claude_command` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:254), `_is_codex_model` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:323), `UnsupportedToolPolicyError` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:331), `apply_tool_policy_to_prompt` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:370), `_build_codex_command` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:386), `_build_agent_command` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:407), `_owner_repo_from_url` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:439), `_substitute_builtins` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:450), `_substitute_inputs` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:476), `_build_context_appendix` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:506), `_build_workspace_prompt` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:514).
- **Repository/store getters**: `get_workflow_repo` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:545), `get_session_repo` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:550), `get_artifact_repo` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:555), `get_publisher` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:560), `_InMemoryAggregateRepository` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:565), `get_trigger_repo` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:596), `get_trigger_store` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:614).
- **GitHub event pipeline wiring** (ADR-050/#602): `get_event_pipeline` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:629), `_create_dedup_adapter` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:656), `_create_import_ledger` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:712), `get_webhook_health_tracker` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:764), `get_pending_sha_store` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:789), `sync_published_events_to_projections` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:840).
- **Execution control / dispatch**: `get_controller` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:872), `BackgroundWorkflowDispatcher` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:924), `get_execute_workflow_handler` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1019), `get_workflow_dispatcher` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1049), `_NullSignalQueueAdapter` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1058).
- **Cost/observability queries**: `get_event_store_instance` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1071), `get_session_cost_query` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1076), `get_execution_cost_query` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1095), `get_canonical_usage_query` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1114), `get_conversation_store` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1133), `get_realtime` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1138), `_get_budget_checker` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1145), `get_subscription_coordinator` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1156), `get_github_settings` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1186).
- **Claude plugin wiring block**: 9 module-level singleton globals plus 14 functions, apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1226-1473, terminated by `reset_claude_plugin_singletons()` at apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1453.
- **Skill wiring block**: 4 module-level singleton globals plus 5 functions, apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1487-1582 (last line of file), terminated by `reset_skill_singletons()` at apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1572.

Singleton state is module-level `_xxx_singleton: T | None = None` globals,
mutated with `global` inside each getter (VERIFIED, e.g.
apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:593, 625-626, 709, 786, 869, 1213-1223,
1481-1484). Two groups (claude plugin, skill) have dedicated
`reset_*_singletons()` functions; the trigger-repo singleton
(`_test_trigger_repo`, apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:593) has no such
function — tests reset it by poking the private module attribute directly
(see Blast radius).

`logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is declared at
apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:921, after several earlier functions in
the file already reference `logger` (VERIFIED by line position relative to
the grep list above — e.g. `_create_dedup_adapter` at line 656 and
`_create_import_ledger` at line 712 precede line 921). This works because
Python resolves module globals at call time, not at parse time, but it means
`logger` is not declared near the top of the file with the other module-level
setup.

Section-boundary comments exist at apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:621-623,
782-784, 864-866, and a longer one at apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1193-1206
that explicitly cites ADR-066 ("See ADR-066: the API tier holds storage +
repository wiring only...", apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1196). The
skill block opens with "Mirrors the claude-plugin wiring block above. Skills
have no global scope..." (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1478) — the
code and its own comments already identify claude-plugin and skill wiring as
a repeated, parallel-structured pattern.

## Is the problem real?

**Partly confirmed.**

1. The file is 1582 lines against the repo's stated global fitness threshold
   of 750 (`max = 750`, fitness.toml:59, VERIFIED). Confirmed on raw line
   count; the exact APSS-measured `metrics.lines_of_code` value used by the
   actual `max-loc-file` check could not be independently verified — see Open
   questions.
2. There is already a grandfathered per-file exception raising the effective
   budget to 1200: `[max-loc-file."apps.syn-api.src.syn_api._wiring"]`,
   `value = 1200`, `issue = "#185"` (fitness-exceptions.toml:48-50,
   VERIFIED). At 1582 raw lines the file exceeds even this grandfathered
   1200-line budget, not just the repo-wide 750 default — so whatever the
   exact measurement basis, this file is very likely failing its own fitness
   gate today, not just the general one.
3. The issue cited by that exception, `#185`, is **not about this file**.
   `gh issue view 185` (VERIFIED, live query) shows #185 is titled
   "refactor(infra): break setup.py into focused modules" and is entirely
   about `infra/scripts/setup.py` (2,284 lines, setup wizard: env files,
   Docker orchestration, Cloudflare tunnels, GitHub App config, 1Password,
   smee.io). It proposes splitting into `infra/scripts/setup/{wizard,env,
   docker,cloudflare,github_app,onepassword,smee}.py`. Nothing in #185
   mentions `_wiring.py`, `syn-api`, or composition roots. So the tracking
   issue attached to the `_wiring.py` exception is factually wrong/stale —
   there is currently no accurate GitHub issue tracking a `_wiring.py`
   size refactor.
4. Separately, `_wiring.py` already carries its own exception in the
   *other* (pytest-based) fitness registry:
   `"apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py" = { max_contexts = 2, issue = "#197" }`
   under `[bounded_context_isolation]` (ci/fitness/fitness_exceptions.toml:20,
   VERIFIED). This is a distinct rule (foreign bounded-context import count,
   not file size) and is evidence the file's breadth-of-concerns problem has
   been flagged before, under a different fitness dimension, tracked to a
   different (also not-obviously-matching-name) issue #197.

Net: the file being oversized is real and measurable by raw line count
against both the global and the grandfathered thresholds. The specific
tracking-issue citation in the size exception is not evidence of anything —
it points at unrelated work. This does not change whether the file is too
big, but it means "the exception already has a plan behind it" is false: as
stated, there is no accurate open issue for this specific refactor.

## What already exists

- **Sibling-module split precedent**: `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring_db.py`
  (61 lines, VERIFIED, full read) already extracts one concern — shared
  asyncpg pool lifecycle (`init_shared_db_pool`, `get_shared_db_pool`,
  `close_shared_db_pool`, module-level `_pool`/`_pool_lock`) — into its own
  `_wiring_<concern>.py` module. `_wiring.py` consumes it via local imports:
  `from syn_api._wiring_db import get_shared_db_pool` inside
  `_create_dedup_adapter` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:656 region)
  and `_create_import_ledger` (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:712
  region) (VERIFIED by grep of both function bodies during earlier reads).
  `_wiring_db.py` is consumed only by `_wiring.py` and
  `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/services/lifecycle.py`
  (grep-VERIFIED, not re-exported to route consumers). This is a working,
  in-repo example of exactly the kind of module split the file itself would
  need, using an underscore-prefixed sibling that is not part of the public
  package surface.
- **Existing internal cohesion boundaries**: the claude-plugin block
  (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1226-1473) and skill block
  (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1487-1582) are self-contained —
  each has its own singleton globals and its own `reset_*_singletons()`
  function, and the skill block's own comment (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:1478)
  states it mirrors the claude-plugin block. The file's own structure already
  marks these as low-coupling, replicable units.
- **`bounded_context_isolation` fitness mechanics** (relevant to any future
  split, not itself a solution): the check
  (ci/fitness/code_quality/test_bounded_context_isolation.py:1-96, VERIFIED,
  full read) counts foreign-bounded-context references using
  `runtime_imports()` (ci/fitness/_imports.py:81-83, VERIFIED, full read),
  which only inspects **module-level** `Import`/`ImportFrom` statements
  (including inside `if`/`try` bodies, ci/fitness/_imports.py:60-70) and
  explicitly excludes `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded imports
  (ci/fitness/_imports.py:25-32, 45). It does *not* use `all_imports()`
  (ci/fitness/_imports.py:86-119), which is the AST-walk variant that also
  catches function-body/lazy imports. `_wiring.py`'s own current pattern for
  cross-module composition (`get_shared_db_pool` imported *inside* function
  bodies, not at module top) is therefore invisible to this particular
  check — a fact any future split would need to account for, since splitting
  `_wiring.py` into files that reference multiple bounded contexts at
  module level (rather than via local/lazy imports) could interact with this
  check differently than the current file does.
- **ADR-066** (docs/adrs/ADR-066-separation-of-concerns.md, VERIFIED, full
  read) names `_wiring.py`/`lifecycle.py` explicitly as the home for
  "Bootstrap and lifecycle wiring" under the principle "Single composition
  root per service" (docs/adrs/ADR-066-separation-of-concerns.md:46). This
  is a constraint on any decomposition, not a solution — the ADR is about
  *which service* wiring belongs to, not about splitting one service's
  wiring file into multiple files.
- **No module-structure-asserting test exists**: a targeted grep for tests
  asserting on `_wiring.py`'s file structure (function count, module split,
  etc.) returned no matches (INFERRED from an empty grep result across the
  test tree; absence-of-evidence, not a full enumeration).
- **No `conftest.py` touches `_wiring` singleton state**: repo-wide search
  for `conftest.py` files found seven
  (`./conftest.py`, `ci/fitness/conftest.py`,
  `ci/fitness/event_sourcing/conftest.py`,
  `packages/syn-adapters/tests/conftest.py`,
  `packages/syn-collector/tests/conftest.py`,
  `packages/syn-domain/src/syn_domain/contexts/organization/slices/conftest.py`,
  `packages/syn-domain/tests/integration/conftest.py`), and none of them
  reference `_wiring` (VERIFIED, `grep -rln "_wiring" --include=conftest.py .`
  returned no matches). `apps/syn-api` has no `conftest.py` at all. So
  singleton reset between tests is handled entirely by the individual test
  files calling `reset_claude_plugin_singletons()` /
  `reset_skill_singletons()` or poking `_test_trigger_repo` directly (see
  Blast radius), not by a shared fixture.

## Blast radius

**Non-test consumers** (34 files under `apps/syn-api/src`, VERIFIED by
`grep -rl "from syn_api\._wiring" apps/syn-api/src`):

- Routes (28 files): `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/routes/artifacts.py`,
  `capture.py`, `claude_plugins.py`, `conversations.py`, `costs.py`,
  `events.py`, `executions/commands.py`, `executions/control.py`,
  `executions/queries.py`, `github.py`, `insights.py`, `metrics.py`,
  `observability.py`, `organizations.py`, `repos.py`, `sessions.py`,
  `skills.py`, `systems.py`, `triggers/commands.py`, `triggers/queries.py`,
  `webhooks/acknowledgments.py`, `webhooks/handlers.py`,
  `webhooks/processing.py`, `webhooks/push_events.py`,
  `webhooks/services.py`, `webhooks/signature.py`, `workflows/commands.py`,
  `workflows/queries.py`.
- Services (5 files): `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/services/credentials.py`,
  `lifecycle.py`, `realtime.py`, `reconciliation.py`, `seeding.py`.

This means essentially every route module in the API imports from
`_wiring.py` — any file split must preserve every one of these import paths
(or update all 33 call sites) without changing behavior.

**Test consumers** (15 files under `apps/syn-api/tests`, VERIFIED by grep):
`integration/test_trigger_scenarios.py`, `test_api_executions.py`,
`test_api_sessions.py`, `test_api_triggers.py`,
`test_claude_plugins_routes.py`,
`test_execute_rejects_unhonourable_declarations.py`,
`test_execution_concurrency_posture.py`, `test_prompt_builtins.py`,
`test_removed_provider_entry_points.py`, `test_skills_install_roundtrip.py`,
`test_skills_read_api.py`, `test_skills_routes.py`,
`test_tool_policy_enforcement.py`, `test_wiring_command_builder.py`,
`test_wiring_telemetry_env.py`.

Of these, two are notable for reaching past the public function surface into
private module state directly:

- `apps/syn-api/tests/integration/test_trigger_scenarios.py:47,93` and
  `apps/syn-api/tests/test_api_triggers.py:26,29` set
  `syn_api._wiring._test_trigger_repo = None` directly (VERIFIED).
- Private (`_`-prefixed) helper functions/classes are imported directly from
  `syn_api._wiring` in: `apps/syn-api/tests/test_removed_provider_entry_points.py:21`
  (`BackgroundWorkflowDispatcher, _build_agent_command`),
  `apps/syn-api/tests/test_prompt_builtins.py:13`
  (`_owner_repo_from_url, _substitute_builtins`),
  `apps/syn-api/tests/test_wiring_telemetry_env.py:13`
  (`_build_workspace_telemetry_env`), and
  `apps/syn-api/tests/test_tool_policy_enforcement.py:46,55,64,74,82`
  (`_build_claude_command`, `UnsupportedToolPolicyError`,
  `_build_agent_command`, imported inline per-test rather than at module
  top) (all VERIFIED). Note `test_wiring_command_builder.py` was in the
  earlier consumer list but its imports were not individually re-verified
  in this pass.

Any decomposition that changes where these private symbols live, or that
relies purely on `_wiring.py` re-exporting names from new sibling modules,
must account for tests that reach into `syn_api._wiring.<private_name>`
directly rather than only through the public function calls.

**ADRs with line-pinned citations into this file** (would go stale after any
line-shifting change, regardless of whether functions move):

- docs/adrs/ADR-069-harness-neutral-phase-definition.md:42 and :49 cite
  `_wiring.py:309` and `_wiring.py:425-433` respectively (grep-VERIFIED line
  existence; surrounding prose not read in this pass).
- docs/adrs/ADR-067-model-registry-and-cost-attribution.md:90 cites
  `_wiring.py:919` (grep-VERIFIED line existence; surrounding prose not read
  in this pass).
- docs/adrs/ADR-060-restart-safe-trigger-deduplication.md:186 and :248
  reference `_wiring.py` generically (not line-pinned) — "Composition root
  (`_wiring.py`)" and a Location line (grep-VERIFIED).
- docs/adrs/ADR-057-declarative-service-lifecycle-registry.md:17 references
  `_wiring.py` generically in prose about issue #596 (grep-VERIFIED).

## Constraints

- **ADR-066** ("Single composition root per service") assigns bootstrap/
  lifecycle wiring to `_wiring.py`/`lifecycle.py` as a pair
  (docs/adrs/ADR-066-separation-of-concerns.md:46, VERIFIED). Any
  decomposition must preserve "one composition root for this service" in
  spirit — i.e., not simply relocate the sprawl into `apps/syn-api/services/`
  or scatter wiring logic across route files, which the ADR's tier table
  explicitly forbids for the API tier ("Long-running work... business rules,
  decision logic" are MUST NOT items for the API tier,
  docs/adrs/ADR-066-separation-of-concerns.md:23).
- **`max-loc-file` fitness rule** (fitness.toml:55-59, VERIFIED) sets a
  750-line default with a per-file exception mechanism
  (fitness-exceptions.toml, APSS format). `_wiring.py` currently has a
  1200-line exception (fitness-exceptions.toml:48-50) that raw line count
  already exceeds.
- **`bounded_context_isolation` fitness rule** (ci/fitness/code_quality/test_bounded_context_isolation.py,
  ci/fitness/fitness_exceptions.toml:20, VERIFIED) currently grandfathers
  `_wiring.py` at `max_contexts = 2`. This rule counts module-level runtime
  imports only (ci/fitness/_imports.py:81-83). It is a live constraint on
  *how* any split is done: new files created from `_wiring.py`'s contents
  would each be evaluated against the *default* `max_contexts = 1` unless
  individually added to the exception registry, since the exception keys are
  per-path (ci/fitness/code_quality/test_bounded_context_isolation.py:75).
- **ADR-060** (restart-safe trigger dedup) governs the Postgres > Redis
  (dedup only) > fail-fast pattern implemented in `_create_dedup_adapter`
  (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:656) and `_create_import_ledger`
  (apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py:712), and is referenced generically
  from `_wiring.py` in that ADR's own text
  (docs/adrs/ADR-060-restart-safe-trigger-deduplication.md:186,248,
  grep-VERIFIED). Any split must not change this fail-fast behavior or the
  `InMemoryAdapter`/`uses_in_memory_stores` gating referenced in CLAUDE.md's
  "In-Memory Adapter Safety (ADR-060)" section.
- **Existing pinned-line ADR citations** (ADR-069:42,49; ADR-067:90, see
  Blast radius) point at specific line numbers inside `_wiring.py` today.
  These are documentation, not enforced by tooling (no fitness check was
  found that validates ADR line citations against source — INFERRED, no
  such check found during this investigation), but they will silently go
  stale if the referenced code moves without the ADRs being updated.
- **CLAUDE.md itself cites `_wiring.py`** in the "In-Memory Adapter Safety
  (ADR-060)" section ("`apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/_wiring.py` -- Adapter
  selection (Postgres > Redis > fail-fast)") — a generic, non-line-pinned
  reference to the file's role, which would remain accurate as long as that
  logic still lives somewhere reachable from this description, even if
  relocated to a sibling module (as `_wiring_db.py` already demonstrates for
  the DB-pool concern).

## Open questions

- **Authoritative APSS `lines_of_code` value for this file.** The
  `max-loc-file` rule is measured from `metrics.lines_of_code` in a
  generated `metrics/modules.json` (fitness.toml:55-59, VERIFIED for the
  rule definition), produced by the Rust `apss-dev` tool
  (`just fitness-check` → `just topology-analyze` → `{{_aps_bin}} run
  architecture-fitness validate .`, INFERRED from justfile target names seen
  earlier in this session, not re-verified in this pass). This tool could
  not be built or run in this environment: `cargo` is not installed
  (`which cargo` → not found, VERIFIED this pass) and outbound access to
  crates.io returned HTTP 403 (VERIFIED this pass,
  `curl -sI https://crates.io` → `HTTP/2 403`), so the registry is
  unreachable even if a toolchain were present. This means the exact
  metric — which may exclude blank lines and/or comments, unlike raw `wc -l`
  — could not be confirmed. **What would settle it**: running
  `just fitness-check` (or the underlying `apss-dev` command) in an
  environment with a working Rust toolchain and network/vendored-crate
  access, or inspecting a checked-in `metrics/modules.json` from a recent CI
  run if one exists (not searched for in this pass).
- **Whether CI is currently red on `main` because of this file specifically.**
  Not directly observed (no CI run log was fetched in this investigation).
  **What would settle it**: `gh run list` / `gh run view` for a recent
  `main` run of the fitness-check workflow, or running `just fitness-check`
  locally if the APSS binary were available.
- **Exact private-symbol test dependencies.** The claim that
  `test_trigger_scenarios.py` and `test_api_triggers.py` set
  `syn_api._wiring._test_trigger_repo = None`, and that five other test
  files import private helpers directly, was established earlier in this
  investigation session but not re-verified with a fresh `Read`/`grep` in
  this final pass. **What would settle it**: `grep -n "_wiring\._test_trigger_repo\|from syn_api\._wiring import _" apps/syn-api/tests/*.py apps/syn-api/tests/integration/*.py`.
- **Whether any other repo (or CI cache) has a prebuilt `apss-dev` binary**
  that could be invoked without a full Rust build. Not searched for in this
  pass beyond a target/release path guess that returned nothing. **What
  would settle it**: a broader filesystem search for an `apss-dev` or
  `aps-dev` binary, or checking whether the fitness-check CI job publishes
  its `metrics/modules.json` as an artifact.
